name: ai.listplus/listplus
title: ListPlus
description: Check B2B leads before you pay to enrich them: 120+ checks with fixes. Then find and enrich leads.

tools.name: what_can_you_do
tools.description: FREE — Use first when you are unsure what ListPlus offers, what something costs or how much budget is left. what ListPlus can do for you: every action, the fields we can fill with their price per record, the free limits, and (with a key) your balance and day budget. With `guide`: one chapter of the manual instead (how — how a list works by itself and what to offer your user —, prices, search, lists, setup, rules, limits, examples).

guide.description: One chapter of the manual as text instead of the overview; `all` = the whole manual

tools.name: find_person
tools.description: PAID (needs a key) — Use when your user names a person, or a role at a company, and wants to know who that is: title, company, LinkedIn profile. 0.5 credits per search, found or not (a fixed price, no estimate; a LinkedIn profile URL alone is not searched and costs nothing) — find a person: name, job title, company, location, LinkedIn profile, how sure. Give first_name + last_name + company (or domain), a LinkedIn URL, a work e-mail, or a question in `query` ("CFO of Tink in Berlin"). No e-mail or phone in the answer — those are enrich_records.

name.description: Full name, when there is no split

domain.description: The company's domain, e.g. acme.com (more exact than the name)

query.description: A question in plain words, e.g. "CFO of Tink in Berlin"

eu_only.description: Only services in the EU (skips one US web index)

tools.name: check_records
tools.description: FREE (up to 25 records without a key, 1000 with one) — Use when your user has contact or company records (a CSV, a CRM export, pasted rows, a few e-mails) and wants to know what is wrong with them. check contact records for errors with 100+ checks: typos in e-mail domains, role mailboxes (office@), duplicates and near-duplicates, phone codes that do not fit the country, LinkedIn status text in names, placeholders … Over MCP the answer is compact: `checks` (what is wrong, with the records' 0-based positions), `fixes` (position → key → the one value to write; "" empties it) and `duplicates` (position to leave out → the position kept, which got what it lacked in its fixes). Have your records their own id? Pass `id_field` and they are named by it. Show your user the changes before you apply them. Nothing is stored or changed.

records.description: Records as JSON objects. Any key names (e.g. first_name, last_name, email, company_name, domain, linkedin_profile_url, job_title, phone, country, city — or Vorname, Firma, Mail …); the answer says how each key was read.

categories.description: Only these areas (any other value is an error)

id_field.description: The key that identifies each of your records (e.g. hs_object_id, a CRM id): the answer names records by its value (`ids`, and as the keys of `fixes` / `duplicates`) instead of their position — safe across calls in parts. Every record needs its own value; the key itself is not checked

view.description: `compact` (the default over MCP): `checks` with positions, `fixes`, `duplicates` — small, for applying. `records` (the default over REST): one entry per record with its findings, messages and from → to — for a person reading it, or an automation working per record. Send `compact` for more than a few hundred records

ai.description: Also run the AI checks (fake names, a person's name as company, department instead of job title, city vs country) — PAID by use, needs a key; never above the `max` this check names in its `options` when called without `ai` (call it so first)

tools.name: enrich_records
tools.description: PAID (needs a key) — Use when records miss a work e-mail, a mobile number, a job title, a LinkedIn profile or company data. per record from a name + company: work e-mail ≈2.39, at most 9 credits; mobile ≈3.84, at most 12; job title ≈1.41, at most 13.5. Charged per hit for e-mail and phone. Use estimate:true first for the exact price of YOUR records (free, no key). Fills fields of contact records (work e-mail, mobile, job title, LinkedIn profile, company, domain, industry, size, place). Send records for a direct result without creating a list, or list_id and record_ids to update shared rows in place. Waits up to 25 s and returns a job_id to poll (get_job) for longer lookups.

records.description: Records as JSON objects. Any key names (e.g. first_name, last_name, email, company_name, domain, linkedin_profile_url, job_title, phone, country, city — or Vorname, Firma, Mail …); the answer says how each key was read.

list_id.description: Enrich rows of this list in place instead of sending records (e.g. the list a search_people answer named)

record_ids.description: With list_id: the rows' ids (`id` in a search answer)

fields.description: Fields to fill: email, phone, job_title, linkedin_profile_url, company_name, domain, industry, city, country

max_credits.description: The most this call may cost (default: the key's day budget left)

estimate.description: true = only the price for these records, nothing runs (free, no key needed)

request_id.description: Your id for this call — a repeat with it gets the same job

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: FREE (key) — Use after enrich_records answered with a job_id, to fetch the result. the state of an enrich_records job; when it ended, the records with the fields we found (in the order you sent them).

job_id.description: The job_id an enrich_records answer handed out

tools.name: verify_email
tools.description: PAID (needs a key) — Use when your user wants to know whether e-mail addresses can receive mail before writing to them; for typos, check_records is free. 0.3 credits per address (an address checked in the last 7 days costs nothing), so a call costs at most its addresses × that — a fixed price, no estimate: is the e-mail address deliverable (valid, invalid, catch_all, unknown)? Up to 25 addresses per call, answered at once.

tools.name: search_options
tools.description: FREE — Use before search_people, count_companies or load_companies, to get the exact filter values. the filters search_people, count_companies and load_companies accept, and the exact values they take (seniorities, departments, company size, industries, countries, states, NAICS codes, revenue …). Without arguments: the categories; with `category`: its values; with `query`: look a word up ("saas", "apparel"). Copy values exactly.

category.description: One category's values, e.g. seniorities, industries, countries, states, naics, employees, revenue (the list: call without arguments)

query.description: Look a word up in the category, e.g. "saas", "apparel", a NAICS code start

parent.description: naics: the code whose children to list (empty = the sectors)

tools.name: count_companies
tools.description: FREE — Use when your user asks how big a market is or how many companies fit a description. how many companies match (market size), e.g. { filters: { countries: ["IT"], naics: ["315"] } }; with `by` (needs a key) broken down by one dimension (countries, states, industries, naics, employees, revenue …). Exact values from search_options (for: companies). Loading the companies into a list is load_companies (priced in `options`).

countries.description: Countries as ISO codes, e.g. US, DE

states.description: States / regions of ONE country (ids; needs exactly one country)

reported_employees.description: Head count classes as the company reports them

company_types.description: Company types, e.g. private, public, nonprofit

categories.description: Business models, e.g. b2b, saas, e-commerce

growth.description: Head count change over 12 months (one value: shrinking, stable, growing, fast)

departments.description: Has a team of at least 5 in each of these departments

exclude.description: Values a company must NOT have — the same keys as the pick filters above

keywords.description: Words describing what the company does (free text); all must fit unless keywords_any

keywords_any.description: true = any of the keywords is enough

technologies.description: Technologies on the company's website, e.g. Shopify, HubSpot; all must fit unless technologies_any

technologies_any.description: true = any of the technologies is enough

name_contains.description: Part of the company's name or domain

founded_min.description: Founded in or after this year

founded_max.description: Founded in or before this year

department.description: search_options category team_departments ("overall" = the whole company)

max.description: At most this many people in it

department.description: search_options category team_departments ("overall" = the whole company)

min_percent.description: Grew by at least this many percent (negative = shrank at most)

filters.description: Company filters. Copy the exact values of each from search_options { for: "companies", category: "<the filter's name>" }

by.description: One dimension to break the total down by: regions, countries, states, industries, sub_industries, naics, employees, reported_employees, revenue, company_types, categories, growth, departments

tools.name: search_people
tools.description: PAID (needs a key) — Use when your user wants new leads: people by role, seniority, industry, place or company. 2 credits per page of up to 25 people, only for pages the database counts (a repeat within 30 days and an empty result cost nothing). Finds people in the B2B people database of our data providers (ListPlus keeps no contact database of its own) by job title, seniority, department, place, industry, company size or company. The people go into a list in ListPlus (name, job title, company, domain, LinkedIn, place — no e-mail or phone: those are enrich_records, priced in `options`). Up to 4 pages per call, a cursor for the next ones (20 pages deep). Exact values from search_options; estimate:true shows the filters as understood and the price (free, no key).

exact_titles.description: true = job titles match exactly, not as "contains"

seniorities.description: Seniorities, e.g. Director, VP, C-Suite — values: search_options category seniorities

departments.description: Departments, e.g. Marketing, Sales — values: search_options category departments

locations.description: Where the PERSON is: cities, countries, territories (DACH, EMEA)

industries.description: The company's industries; everyday words like saas or fintech are understood — values: search_options category industries

headcount.description: The company's size class, e.g. 51-100 — values: search_options category headcount

company_domains.description: Company domains, e.g. acme.com (more exact than names)

has_email.description: Only people the database holds a verified work e-mail for

has_mobile.description: Only people the database holds a verified mobile number for

pages.description: Pages of up to 25 to load in this call (default 1)

cursor.description: From the last answer: the next pages of the same search into the same list

list_id.description: Append to this list of the workspace (default: a new list per search)

max_credits.description: The most this call may cost; it loads fewer pages / refuses rather than spend more

estimate.description: true = the filters as understood and the price, nothing runs (free, no key)

tools.name: load_companies
tools.description: PAID (needs a key) — Use when your user wants the companies of a market as a list, after count_companies sized it. 0.25 credits per company delivered (25 companies = 6.25 credits): the companies a count_companies question found, into a company list in ListPlus — name, domain, website, industry, size, place, LinkedIn page. 10, 25, 50 per call (`limit`), a cursor for the next ones. The same page within an hour costs nothing again. estimate:true shows the price (free, no key).

tools.name: describe_list
tools.description: FREE (key) — Use first whenever your user refers to one of their ListPlus lists: it names the lists you may work on and what you may do there. without list_id: the lists shared with you (name, kind, rows, what you may do). With list_id: its columns (content types, allowed values, which you may write), statuses, the sublists you are limited to, the pipelines you may hand records to, the filter conditions, and the tools this list allows. Call it before working on a list.

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list without list_id shows the lists shared with you)

tools.name: query_records
tools.description: FREE (key) — Use to read, filter or count the records of a ListPlus list. read records of a list shared with you: `mode` rows (default; columns you may see, each with id and url), count, or ids (up to 10,000, to pass on as record_ids). Filter by column values or conditions (describe_list names them).

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list without list_id shows the lists shared with you)

filter.description: Column → value: exact, { "contains": "…" }, { "not": "…" }, { "is_empty": true } or { "condition": "<one of filter_conditions>" }; ar_status by status name

logic.description: How several filter entries combine (default and)

columns.description: Only these columns in the rows

limit.description: Rows per call (capped by the list's share, default 100)

include_hidden.description: Also records hidden in the list (status "ignored")

tools.name: add_records
tools.description: FREE (key) — Use when your user wants records kept in a ListPlus list. add records to a list shared with you for editing. Use the record fields below (they are ListPlus's names — do not send your own headers) and the list's other columns by name (describe_list). A record the list already has (same e-mail, LinkedIn, name + company) is filled in, not doubled. Up to 1,000 per call. The answer says what was understood, kept (`keptFields`, `hints`) and, in your own list, made a column (`createdColumns`).

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list without list_id shows the lists shared with you)

full_name.description: Whole name, only when you do not have the parts: "First Last" or "Last, First" — ListPlus splits it

email.description: The person's work e-mail — only one you READ at a source; never built from a name (ListPlus finds it)

linkedin_profile_url.description: The person's profile (linkedin.com/in/…) — only one you opened; never guessed (ListPlus finds it)

company_name.description: The company the person works at

company_domain.description: The company's own domain (acme.com). Leave empty unless you know it — ListPlus finds it; never a source's domain

company_website.description: The company's own website — never a profile, an article or a directory page

source_url.description: Where you found the record (article, post, profile, directory) — stored as the source, never as a website

note.description: Free text about the record (why it fits)

records.description: The records: the record fields below, and the list's other columns by name

dry_run.description: true: write nothing, answer how the records would be stored

request_id.description: Your id for this call — a repeat with it writes nothing twice

tools.name: update_records
tools.description: FREE (key) — Use when values in a ListPlus list should change. change cells of a list shared with you for editing: per record (`records: [{ id, column: value }]`) or one change for many (`record_ids` or `filter` + `set`). Only the columns you may write (describe_list); `only_empty` fills empty cells only.

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list without list_id shows the lists shared with you)

filter.description: Column → value: exact, { "contains": "…" }, { "not": "…" }, { "is_empty": true } or { "condition": "<one of filter_conditions>" }; ar_status by status name

set.description: With record_ids or filter: column → new value

tools.name: mark_records
tools.description: FREE (key) — Use to qualify, tag or put aside records of a ListPlus list (status, tags, hide). set a status (one of the list's, "" clears it — may start the list's rules, as in the app), add or remove tags, or hide records (restorable; hide: false shows them again) in a list shared with you for editing. Nothing is deleted.

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list without list_id shows the lists shared with you)

filter.description: Column → value: exact, { "contains": "…" }, { "not": "…" }, { "is_empty": true } or { "condition": "<one of filter_conditions>" }; ar_status by status name

status.description: A status name of the list (describe_list), or "" to clear

hide.description: true = hide in the list (restorable), false = show again

tools.name: check_list
tools.description: FREE (key) — Use when your user asks about the data quality of a ListPlus list. run the 100+ data-quality checks on a list shared with you (or on some of its records): a score, the findings per check with the affected record ids and a proposed fix each (fix_list applies one).

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list without list_id shows the lists shared with you)

categories.description: Only these areas (any other value is an error)

tools.name: fix_list
tools.description: FREE (key) — Use after check_list, once your user agreed to apply fixes, clean values or merge duplicates. apply ONE of: a check's proposed fixes (`check_id` from check_list), cleaning values (trim, casing, placeholders — `clean_values: true`), or merging duplicates (`dedup_key`: email, name_company, linkedin, phone, name — merged rows are hidden, not deleted). Needs editing on the list.

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list without list_id shows the lists shared with you)

clean_values.description: true = clean values of the given columns / all

dedup_key.description: Merge duplicates found by this key

tools.name: derive_column
tools.description: PAID (needs a key) — Use when a column should be filled by AI from other columns (the gender from the first name, a seniority from the job title). AI tokens by use (usually cents; at most 10 credits per call, within the key's day budget): fill an existing column from others by an instruction (e.g. the gender from the first name, a seniority from the job title, a country from the city). Unique values are asked once.

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list without list_id shows the lists shared with you)

description.description: What to put in, e.g. "male, female or unknown from the first name"

filter.description: Column → value: exact, { "contains": "…" }, { "not": "…" }, { "is_empty": true } or { "condition": "<one of filter_conditions>" }; ar_status by status name

tools.name: copy_records
tools.description: FREE (key) — Use to copy or move records between two ListPlus lists. copy records from one list shared with you into another (same kind: contacts or companies) — with `move: true` they are then hidden in the source (restorable, never deleted). A record the target already has is filled in, not doubled; a copy never goes back into a list it came through. Up to 1,000 per call.

filter.description: Column → value: exact, { "contains": "…" }, { "not": "…" }, { "is_empty": true } or { "condition": "<one of filter_conditions>" }; ar_status by status name

move.description: true = hide the records in the source after the copy

tools.name: send_to_pipeline
tools.description: FREE (key) to hand over — Use when records should go to the CRM, a sequencer or Slack through one of the workspace's pipelines. records of a list shared with you go to one of the workspace's pipelines you may use (describe_list names them: HubSpot, Slack, lemlist …). The pipeline's data check and release apply: a manual one waits for a person; one that sends by itself delivers at once and is PAID per record delivered — describe_list names each pipeline's `credits_per_record`; it counts on this key's day budget. Tell your user records × that price first. Up to 500 per call.

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list without list_id shows the lists shared with you)

filter.description: Column → value: exact, { "contains": "…" }, { "not": "…" }, { "is_empty": true } or { "condition": "<one of filter_conditions>" }; ar_status by status name

tools.name: describe_setup
tools.description: FREE (key, Set up) — Use before you build or change a list's columns or rules. what you need before you set something up. Without list_id: whether this connection may set up, the column kinds and the limits. With list_id: the list's columns (kinds), statuses, rules (triggers), the fields a condition may use with their operators, the pipelines you may hand records to, and the connected HubSpot, Salesforce and Attio accounts. Call it before add_column or create_trigger.

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list shows the lists shared with you)

language.description: Language of `tell_your_user` and of Yes/No words in new columns (default en)

tools.name: create_list
tools.description: FREE (key, Set up) — Use when your user wants a new list in their workspace. a new list in the workspace (contacts or companies), with the standard columns of its kind (what an enrichment fills later) plus the content types you name, and optional statuses. It is this agent's own list: shared in Full. Then add_column, create_trigger, add_records.

columns.description: More content types, placed first (lead_score, department …) — the standard columns are always there

language.description: Language of `tell_your_user` and of Yes/No words in new columns (default en)

tools.name: add_column
tools.description: FREE (key, Set up) to set up — Use when a list needs a new column: a score, a label, a lookup, a formula or an AI column. plain, select, formula, rule-based score / label, lookup, in_list and job_change columns cost nothing (Edit on the list). A hubspot column (or salesforce, attio: in that CRM? Yes / No) is PAID: 1 credit per request of up to 100 values (Salesforce, Attio: 50), for the first run and later records. AI criteria in a score and ai_text columns are PAID: 0.02 credits per AI answer (unique values once), Full on the list; their first run costs at most the list's records × that and counts on this connection's day budget, later records run under the list's own day limit. Tell your user the price before you add a paid column. Up to 10 columns per call; call describe_setup first for the fields a rule may use.

formula.description: The app's formula language; columns as {Column title}

when.description: The rule (columns, content types, reference lists, job change)

field.description: A field exactly as describe_setup names it, e.g. { "kind": "contentType", "key": "job_title" }, { "kind": "column", "name": "score" }, { "kind": "status" }, { "kind": "tags" }

op.description: An operator describe_setup offers for that field

ai.description: …or a statement the AI judges per record (paid, Full)

field.description: A field exactly as describe_setup names it, e.g. { "kind": "contentType", "key": "job_title" }, { "kind": "column", "name": "score" }, { "kind": "status" }, { "kind": "tags" }

op.description: An operator describe_setup offers for that field

values.description: The first value whose rule is met wins

tools.name: remove_column
tools.description: FREE (key, Set up, Full on the list) — Use when a column should go from a list. remove a column from a list (by name or title). Records are never deleted; ask your user before you remove a column a person made.

list_id.description: The list's id (describe_list shows the lists shared with you)

language.description: Language of `tell_your_user` and of Yes/No words in new columns (default en)

tools.name: create_trigger
tools.description: FREE (key, Set up) to set up — Use when something should happen by itself whenever a record arrives, changes or meets a condition. a rule (trigger) of a list: when a record is new / changed / meets the conditions, set a status (a new name is created), add a tag, hide it (it leaves the normal flow: no checks, rules, enrichment or sync — restorable), hand it to an EXISTING pipeline (pipelines are made by a person in the app), or ENRICH it — PAID: the cheapest route first (often 0 credits), dearer ones only after a miss, mostly per hit; budget_per_record is a CEILING per record, not its price; on THIS connection's day budget (an empty day makes the rule wait, never overspend). Active at once unless activate: false — set an enrich rule up paused until your user agreed to the budget. include_existing runs it once for the records already in the list. Status, tag and hide need Edit on the list; a pipeline the pipeline's share; enrich Full. Call describe_setup first for the fields and operators.

field.description: A field exactly as describe_setup names it, e.g. { "kind": "contentType", "key": "job_title" }, { "kind": "column", "name": "score" }, { "kind": "status" }, { "kind": "tags" }
